name: Hohe Salve
kurzbeschreibung: The Hohe Salve at 1,828 m in the Kitzb?heler Alpen: Tyrol's finest panoramic mountain featuring the Salvenkirchlein, a rotating terrace, and views of 70 three-thousanders.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Hohe Salve is a prominent, freestanding pyramid-shaped mountain rising to an elevation of 1,828 metres in the Kitzb?heler Alpen in the Tyrolean Unterland. Located between the Brixental, S?llandl, and the Inntal, this peak is respectfully referred to in popular parlance as the 'Rigi of Tyrol'. Thanks to its exposed, isolated position, the Hohe Salve offers one of the most stunning 360-degree summit panoramas in all of Central Europe: the vista encompasses more than 70 snow-capped three-thousand-metre peaks ? from the Gro?glockner and Gro?venediger across the Zillertal Alps to the rugged limestone precipices of the Wilder Kaiser and the Bavarian Prealps.

Salvenkirchlein & Attractions

The mountain's history as a sacred cult site dates back to pre-Christian eras. Gracing the highest point is the world-famous Salvenkirchlein (officially dedicated to Saint John the Baptist): first recorded in documents in 1589, this whitewashed chapel with its onion dome is the highest pilgrimage church in all of Austria. For centuries, farmers and pilgrims have journeyed here on the patron saint's day to pray for favourable weather and bountiful harvests. Inside, visitors are captivated by a Baroque altar and a life-sized statue of the church patron. A technological highlight at the summit is the Gipfelrestaurant Hohe Salve with Austria's first revolving panoramic terrace: the circular platform rotates imperceptibly and silently through a full 360 degrees within about 45 minutes, allowing diners a seamless all-round view while eating. The alpine experience is complemented by the interactive Sonnenuhren-Erlebniswelt (sundial experience world) featuring 15 art and time stations that vividly illustrate ancient celestial timekeeping in the high mountains.

Visit & Getting There

The Hohe Salve is accessible continuously daily from 08:30 to 17:00 via modern cable cars in summer (late May to late October) and winter (December to April). Summer cable car fares (2025/2026 season): ascent and descent adults approx. ?33.50, youth approx. ?25.00, children (born 2009?2018) approx. ?17.00; toddlers ride for free. Access to the summit plateau, the Salvenkirchlein, and the sundial trail is free of charge with a valid mountain railway ticket. Holders of the Kitzb?heler Alpen Sommer Card or the SkiWelt Erlebnis-Wanderpass travel free. Arrival by cable car: Ride up either with the modern gondolas from Hopfgarten im Brixental or from S?ll directly to the summit station. Arrival by train: The ?BB railway station Hopfgarten Berglift is located just 150 metres from the valley station. By car: Via the B178 or B170 to Hopfgarten or S?ll to the large free parking lots at the cable car stations.

Tips

The gondola lifts from Hopfgarten and S?ll up to the summit as well as the revolving panoramic terrace are exemplarily barrier-free and accessible for wheelchairs; the circular path around the summit plateau is also flat and suitable for pushchairs. Plan to have lunch on the rotating observation deck and sample authentic Tyrolean Germkn?del or Kaiserschmarrn while gazing out towards the Gro?glockner.
